as_told.title: Kennedy-Khrushchev secret letters on nuclear disarmament lead Dulles and Brown Brothers Harriman to target JFK

plain: President John F. Kennedy, the story goes, set up secret lines of contact with the Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev in the 1960s to ease tensions and cut back nuclear weapons, while men inside his own government wanted him gone. Michels frames it this way himself: Kennedy was reaching for détente and denuclearization, and Allen Dulles, the head of the CIA (the US spy agency) whom Kennedy had fired, "basically wanted to take him out." A guest named Dan Sheehan, from an episode titled "The Man Involved In Every American Conspiracy," passes on what he was told by a man named Walter Sullivan. Sheehan says the two leaders exchanged 18 letters "completely secretly outside of the channels of the state department" and outside the CIA, and he ties the Wall Street bank Brown Brothers Harriman to the targeting of Kennedy. If true, it would mean Kennedy's push for peace made him dangerous enemies at home.
